name: Question 3
problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{4},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
We require a $4\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x+(-3)y+0z \\ 1x+(-2)y+1z \\ 0x+0y+0z \\ 0x+0y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

a
[7100−3−2100101]
b
[7−301−21000001]

[7−301−21001]

[000000000000]

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We require a 4×3 matrix T such that T⋅[xyz]=[7x+(−3)y+0z1x+(−2)y+1z0x+0y+0z0x+0y+1z].

Notice that [7−301−21000001]⋅[xyz]=[7x−3yx−2y+z0z]. Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation T is [7−301−21000001].
